_readme: Layered knowledge base: religion base + optional regional variant. Day offsets are relative to the main wedding day (0). confidence = high|medium|low. This file never contains auspicious dates; timing questions go to the person in confirm_with. Verify every item with your family's religious authority.

functions.name: Haldi
rituals: Turmeric paste applied by family members

functions.name: Wedding Ceremony (Vivah)
rituals: Mangalsutra or sindoor, depending on region

functions.name: Reception
rituals: Dinner and blessings for the new couple

dietary.rule: Many families serve vegetarian food at religious functions and avoid alcohol there; practice varies by family.

dress.rule: Traditional Indian attire is the norm. Many families avoid black at ceremonies.

timing.rule: Ceremony timings are set by the family pandit, not by this app.

who_pays.rule: Traditionally the bride's family hosts the wedding and the groom's family hosts the reception; many modern families split costs.

task_templates.title: Plan the engagement gathering and guest list
Confirm ceremony details and samagri (ritual items) list with your pandit
Decide who performs which ritual roles (kanyadaan, pheras)
Plan Mehndi timing and henna
Arrange turmeric, flowers and outfits for Haldi

functions.name: Walima
rituals: Feast hosted by the groom's family

dress.rule: Modest dress. Some families arrange separate seating for men and women; ask your families.

timing.rule: Ask your imam about timing, including whether any period such as Ramadan affects your plan.

who_pays.rule: The groom gives the mahr to the bride (required). The Walima is hosted by the groom's family. The nikah meal is often hosted by the bride's family but this varies.

task_templates.title: Agree on the mahr and speak with the imam/qazi about the nikah
Confirm two witnesses and nikahnama paperwork
Plan the Walima guest list and halal catering

dietary.rule: Langar and the gurdwara premises are vegetarian and free of alcohol and tobacco.

dress.rule: Everyone covers their head in the gurdwara; modest dress.

timing.rule: Anand Karaj is usually held in the morning; confirm availability with the gurdwara and granthi.

who_pays.rule: No fixed rule; families usually agree on this together.

task_templates.title: Book the gurdwara and speak with the granthi
Confirm laavan readers, kirtan and langar arrangements
Plan the engagement (Kurmai) gathering

functions.name: Church Wedding
rituals: Blessing by the priest or pastor

dietary.rule: No fixed rules; alcohol is common at receptions.

dress.rule: Bride often wears white or ivory; guests dress modestly for church.

timing.rule: Church scheduling, pre-marriage preparation and banns can take months and differ by denomination; confirm early with your priest or pastor.

who_pays.rule: Traditionally the bride's family; many couples now split costs.

task_templates.title: Book the church and meet your priest/pastor; ask about the pre-marriage course and banns
Choose readings, hymns and wedding party roles
Plan the ring ceremony

functions.name: Engagement
rituals: Family meeting and exchange of gifts

functions.name: Buddhist Wedding Ceremony
rituals: Blessing and chanting by a monk

dietary.rule: Many families keep the ceremony meal vegetarian and alcohol-free; varies widely.

dress.rule: Simple, modest dress; light colours are common.

timing.rule: Depends on the monk's availability; ask your monk.

task_templates.title: Meet the monk to plan the blessing and vows

dietary.rule: Strictly vegetarian with no root vegetables (such as onion, garlic, potato); no alcohol.

dress.rule: Modest dress; leather is avoided in temples.

timing.rule: Many observant families finish meals before sunset; plan food timings with your families.

task_templates.title: Speak with your vidhikarak/pandit about the ceremony and Jain dietary rules for every function
Brief the caterer: no root vegetables, meals before sunset

functions.name: Jaggo
rituals: Decorated pot of lamps carried through the neighbourhood

functions.name: Chooda & Kalire
rituals: Red and ivory bangles presented by the maternal uncle's family

functions.name: Baraat & Milni
rituals: Milni: formal meeting of the two families with gifts

dietary.rule: Non-vegetarian food and alcohol are common at Sangeet and Reception in many families, but a gurdwara ceremony venue is vegetarian and dry.

dress.rule: Bright colours; red is common for the bride.

timing.rule: The wedding day tends to start early (chooda, baraat, milni, then the ceremony).

who_pays.rule: The bride's family traditionally hosts the wedding; the groom's family often hosts the Sangeet or Reception.

task_templates.title: Plan Sangeet performances and music
Prepare the jaggo pot and invite neighbours
Arrange chooda and kalire with the maternal uncle's family
Plan the milni (who meets whom, gift list)

functions.name: Pithi
rituals: Turmeric and sandalwood paste applied to the bride and groom at their own homes

functions.name: Graha Shanti Puja
rituals: Prayers for the couple, led by the pandit

dietary.rule: Gujarati wedding menus are almost always vegetarian and alcohol is rarely served; Jain families keep it stricter.

dress.rule: Chaniya choli and kediyu are popular for Garba night; bright colours.

timing.rule: Garba night is usually the evening before the wedding.

who_pays.rule: The bride's family traditionally hosts the wedding meal; varies in practice.

task_templates.title: Plan Garba/Sangeet music and dress-code note for guests
Arrange pithi supplies at each home
Plan the jaan and ponkhvu welcome

functions.name: Reception
rituals: Reception on the evening before the ceremony is common

dietary.rule: Traditional wedding meals are vegetarian, served on banana leaf.

dress.rule: Silk saree (often Kanjeevaram) for the bride; veshti and angavastram for the groom.

timing.rule: Ceremony timings are set by the priest; ask them early.

who_pays.rule: Varies by family; the bride's family often hosts the main wedding meal.

task_templates.title: Confirm Kasi Yatra, oonjal and thali arrangements with your priest
Plan the reception evening
Plan Nalangu games and family roles

functions.name: Aashirbaad (Blessing)
rituals: Elders bless the bride and groom with gifts, paddy and durba grass

functions.name: Aiburobhaat
rituals: Last bachelor meal at each home, cooked by family

functions.name: Gaye Holud
rituals: Turmeric sent from the other side with fish, sweets and a saree

functions.name: Bou Bhaat (Reception)
rituals: Feast hosted by the groom's family for the new bride

dietary.rule: Fish is traditional at many Bengali Hindu feasts and in gaye holud gifts; plan vegetarian alternatives for guests who do not eat it.

dress.rule: Red and white saree (or red Benarasi) for the bride; dhoti-panjabi and topor for the groom.

timing.rule: The couple traditionally fast until the ceremony in many families; ask your purohit.

who_pays.rule: The bride's family hosts the wedding; the groom's family hosts Bou Bhaat.

task_templates.title: Plan Gaye Holud trays at each home (turmeric, fish, sweets, saree)
Plan Aiburobhaat meals at each home
Plan Bou Bhaat hosted by the groom's family
Fix Aashirbaad date and family gifts

functions.name: Kelvan
rituals: Pre-wedding feast hosted by relatives for the couple

functions.name: Halad Chadavne
rituals: Turmeric applied by married women of the family

functions.name: Simant Puja
rituals: Bride's family welcomes the groom's family

dietary.rule: Ceremony meals are commonly vegetarian; confirm with both families.

dress.rule: Nauvari (nine-yard) saree for the bride; dhoti and pheta (turban) for the groom are traditional.

timing.rule: Ceremony timing is set by the priest.

who_pays.rule: The bride's family traditionally hosts the wedding; varies in practice.

task_templates.title: Arrange nauvari saree, dhoti and pheta
Plan Simant Puja welcome
Plan the Kelvan feasts

functions.name: Dholki
rituals: Evenings of singing with a dholak at each home

functions.name: Rukhsati
rituals: Bride's farewell from her parents' home

dietary.rule: All food halal; large biryani-style meals are typical.

dress.rule: Modest dress; sherwani or shalwar for men and heavy lehenga or sharara for brides are common.

who_pays.rule: Mahr from the groom is required; Walima hosted by the groom's family.

task_templates.title: Plan Dholki evenings at each home
Plan the rukhsati moment with both families

generic_tasks.title: Agree on the total budget and who pays for which function
Draft the guest list for each side
Meet your {confirm_with} to confirm ritual details and timings
Check marriage registration requirements and paperwork
Collect RSVPs and finalise headcount per function
Confirm outfits are fitted and ready
Share final headcount with the caterer and venue
Prepare gift envelopes and a day-of schedule for family
